subject: Activation of fallback ladder & request for evidence from NimbleRetail - dedicated pool incident
summary: Dedicated GPU pool experienced sudden queue amplification causing elevated tail latency for NimbleRetail. Engineering activated the fallback ladder to throttle noncritical batches and provided immediate mitigation; requesting customer confirmation and additional logs for post-incident reconciliation.
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, ops@nimble-retail.com
Date: 2026-11-12T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: [Urgent] Dedicated pool queue amplification impacting NimbleRetail - immediate fallback activated

Team / NimbleRetail ops,

We observed an abrupt increase in small short-lived jobs that amplified the hot-queue for the NimbleRetail dedicated pool (pool-id: rdw-ded-nr-01) starting at ~08:30 PT. This produced elevated tail latency and increased error rates for long-running inference sessions.

What we did immediately:
- Activated the fallback ladder for the tenant (fallback -> reduced-batch, prefix-KV pinning, and routing to warm-standby model variant).
- Throttled noncritical autopromote jobs for 20 minutes to drain the queue.
- Rolled a targeted config to limit very short-lived fanout (rate cap at 250 qps per shard).

Visible customer impact: minor increases in 95th/99th latency for production endpoints; a small subset of long-running streams saw transient failures and reconnects.

Attachments: queue_snapshot_08-45.png (screenshot of pending queue at 08:45), allocator_logs_20261112.tar.gz (collector).

Next steps: we're preparing a short evidence packet and a proposed SLA-bridge credit. Markus / Marissa, I’ve looped you for customer comms. NimbleRetail, could you confirm whether you saw increased client-side retries during this window and whether you can share the application request IDs for the errors (if available)?

Thanks,
Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

--

Hi Sarah / NimbleRetail team,

First, apologies for the disruption this morning — I appreciate the quick patience from your side while we stabilized the pool. To be explicit about our actions and commitments:

1) We activated the fallback ladder to preserve stream integrity for your latency-sensitive endpoints; noncritical tasks were deprioritized so your customer-facing requests could continue.
2) We captured allocator and queue snapshots and are preparing an evidence package for your review (link below).
3) As a remediation step, we are proposing a one-time SLA-bridge credit while we finish the post-incident analysis. Attached is the draft SLA-bridge proposal (sla-bridge-proposal-20261112.pdf).

Request for you:
- Please share any request IDs or sample logs for failed streams (client-side). That will help us correlate traces.
- If you prefer a live review, I can set up a 30-minute post-incident sync today at 10:30 PT.

We’ll follow up with a short RCA and mitigation plan by EOD.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: [Urgent] Dedicated pool queue amplification impacting NimbleRetail - immediate fallback activated

Hi all,

Quick technical note before the sync: initial traces show a fanout of a lightweight batch job that did not respect per-tenant rate limits; it caused repeated micro-jobs that occupied hot-shard slots. We limited backfill and applied a temporary per-shard qps cap while we drain.

Attached: allocator_logs_20261112.tar.gz (contains master allocator trace, shard queue dump, and per-tenant throttle events). I also included a small script (extract_top_keys.sh) and a brief README describing correlation points.

Planned follow-ups we will deliver in the RCA:
- Root cause: why the fanout bypassed tenant rate-limiting (suspected regression in batch-coordinator).
- Concrete mitigation: canary for batch-coordinator fix, stronger rejection rather than queueing for short-lived micro-jobs, and a global hot-queue cap.
- Timeline: hotfix to be staged tomorrow (2026-11-13) with rollout by 2026-11-15 pending test results.

If NimbleRetail can share the ops-ids.csv and any client-side traces ahead of the sync, we’ll annotate our traces for precise correlation.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal SW Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
